I found both implementations and where the display names come from.

- For local STT:
  - list function just maps predefined models to info.
  - The display name comes from `WhisperModel::display_name()` or `AmModel::display_name()` via `SupportedSttModel::info()`.

```15:27:plugins/local-stt/src/commands.rs
#[tauri::command]
#[specta::specta]
pub async fn list_supported_models() -> Result<Vec<SttModelInfo>, String> {
    Ok(SUPPORTED_MODELS.iter().map(|m| m.info()).collect())
}
```

```198:216:plugins/local-stt/src/model.rs
pub fn info(&self) -> SttModelInfo {
    match self {
        SupportedSttModel::Whisper(model) => SttModelInfo {
            key: self.clone(),
            display_name: model.display_name().to_string(),
            size_bytes: model.model_size_bytes(),
        },
        SupportedSttModel::Am(model) => SttModelInfo {
            key: self.clone(),
            display_name: model.display_name().to_string(),
            size_bytes: model.model_size_bytes(),
        },
        SupportedSttModel::Custom(_) => SttModelInfo {
            key: self.clone(),
            display_name: "Custom".to_string(),
            size_bytes: 0,
        },
    }
}
```

- For local LLM:
  - The list function returns a hardcoded vector with names inlined.

```15:36:plugins/local-llm/src/commands.rs
#[tauri::command]
#[specta::specta]
pub async fn list_supported_model() -> Result<Vec<ModelInfo>, String> {
    Ok(vec![
        ModelInfo {
            key: SupportedModel::HyprLLM,
            name: "HyprLLM".to_string(),
            description: "Experimental model trained by the Hyprnote team.".to_string(),
            size_bytes: SupportedModel::HyprLLM.model_size(),
        },
        ModelInfo {
            key: SupportedModel::Gemma3_4bQ4,
            name: "Gemma 3 4B Q4".to_string(),
            description: "Deprecated. Exists only for backward compatibility.".to_string(),
            size_bytes: SupportedModel::Gemma3_4bQ4.model_size(),
        },
        ModelInfo {
            key: SupportedModel::Llama3p2_3bQ4,
            name: "Llama 3.2 3B Q4".to_string(),
            description: "Deprecated. Exists only for backward compatibility.".to_string(),
            size_bytes: SupportedModel::Llama3p2_3bQ4.model_size(),
        },
    ])
}
```

Status: I looked up both commands and traced how names are derived.

I checked both sides.

- For local LLM: the built‑in list is only three models (HyprLLM, Gemma 3 4B Q4, Llama 3.2 3B Q4). Tongyi/Phi 4 don’t come from here.
```15:35:plugins/local-llm/src/commands.rs
pub async fn list_supported_model() -> Result<Vec<ModelInfo>, String> {
    Ok(vec![
        ModelInfo { key: SupportedModel::HyprLLM, name: "HyprLLM".to_string(), ... },
        ModelInfo { key: SupportedModel::Gemma3_4bQ4, name: "Gemma 3 4B Q4".to_string(), ... },
        ModelInfo { key: SupportedModel::Llama3p2_3bQ4, name: "Llama 3.2 3B Q4".to_string(), ... },
    ])
}
```

- The “many more” models (e.g., Tongyi/Qwen, Phi‑4, Mistral, Yi, GLM, etc.) come from the Custom Endpoint flow:
  - OpenRouter: a small hardcoded list is shown in the dropdown (can include various third‑party models), but it’s not exhaustive.
  - Others: the app dynamically calls your configured OpenAI‑compatible API’s `/models` endpoint and lists whatever it returns (`data[].id`). That’s where Tongyi/Qwen and Phi‑4 show up if your endpoint exposes them.
```209:265:apps/desktop/src/components/settings/components/ai/llm-custom-view.tsx
const othersModels = useQuery({
  queryKey: ["others-direct-models", debouncedApiBase, debouncedApiKey?.slice(0, 8)],
  queryFn: async (): Promise<string[]> => {
    const url = new URL(apiBase);
    url.pathname += url.pathname.endsWith("/") ? "models" : "/models";
    const response = await tauriFetch(url.toString(), { method: "GET", headers });
    const data = await response.json();
    const models = data.data
      .map((model: any) => model.id)
      .filter((id: string) => !["dall-e", "codex", "whisper"].some(k => id.includes(k)));
    return models;
  },
  enabled: /* valid URL + (local or api key) */,
});
```

So:
- Local tab = only the three built‑in models.
- Custom tab = model names are provided by the external provider (OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, or any OpenAI‑compatible “Others” base). Tongyi/Qwen, Phi‑4, etc., appear when that provider’s `/models` endpoint lists them.

Status: I traced local vs custom model sources and verified the dynamic `/models` fetch.
